title: RecordHeader
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.material3.TopAppBar with MonarchIconButton and MonarchMenu, androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column and FlowRow, MonarchTabs, with MonarchAvatar, MonarchInlineEditText, MonarchStatusBadge, MonarchBadge, MonarchKeyValue and MonarchCalloutBanner
summary: The header of a record screen, such as a contact, ticket or deal: the title, back, previous and next and the More menu in the top app bar, and under it the avatar, editable title, status and badges, key facts, a state banner and section tabs.
whenToUse: At the top of a record's detail screen in a CRM, help desk or admin app, under the screen's TopAppBar.
whenNotToUse: Not for the header of a list or a settings page; use a TopAppBar with MonarchSectionHeader. Not for a summary of a record in a list; use MonarchCard.
api: TopAppBar(title = { Text(name, maxLines = 1, overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis) }, navigationIcon = { MonarchIconButton(label = "Back to contacts", onClick = back) { … } }, actions = { MonarchIconButton(label = "Previous contact", onClick = previous, enabled = index > 0) { … }; MonarchIconButton(label = "Next contact", onClick = next, enabled = index < lastIndex) { … }; Box { MonarchIconButton(label = "More actions for $name", onClick = { menuOpen = true }) { … }; MonarchMenu(expanded = menuOpen, onDismissRequest = { menuOpen = false }) { MonarchMenuItem(…) } } })

Row { MonarchAvatar(image, name, size = MonarchAvatarSize.Lg, decorative = true); MonarchInlineEditText(value = name, onSave = …, label = "Contact name", modifier = Modifier.weight(1f).semantics { heading() }) }
MonarchTabs(selectedIndex = currentTab, onSelectedIndexChange = { currentTab = it }) { tab(…) }

options.name: TopAppBar.actions

appearance: Each part keeps its own component's color roles: the avatar's fallback colors, badges in their tones, facts in the muted and default text colors, the banner in its tone, and the tab row's accent indicator. The top app bar takes the Monarch Material color scheme in every theme.
platformNotes: The web RecordHeader is one component with slots for back link, previous and next, avatar, title, badges, facts, actions, banner and tabs. On Android, as on iOS, the back button, the title and the actions belong to the top app bar, so Monarch ships a recipe instead of a type: back, previous, next and More are MonarchIconButtons in TopAppBar, record actions are a MonarchMenu, and the rest is composed under it in the screen's scrolling Column. The web's position text "3 of 40" is plain caption text. The heading level option has no Android meaning; the editable title carries heading semantics. Monarch bundles no icons; the example uses framework drawables.
accessibility: The back, previous, next and More buttons are MonarchIconButtons with 48dp targets, named after the record type and the record: "Previous contact", "More actions for Ada Lovelace".
The editable title has heading semantics, so TalkBack's heading navigation reaches it.

Each composed component keeps its own accessibility: status and badges read their text, facts are read as label and value pairs, the banner is read with its tone, and the tabs are tabs with their selected state.
Everything wraps and grows with the font size setting; the top app bar title is cut to one line by the system and stays in full in the header.
edgeCases: A long title wraps in the header and is truncated in the top app bar.
Many badges wrap onto new lines in the FlowRow.
On the first and last record the previous and next buttons are disabled.
With no facts, leave MonarchKeyValue out rather than passing an empty list.
